chunks: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying to one of the companions of Qays al-Masir:

Indeed, God the Mighty and Majestic educated His Prophet, and excellent was His education of him. When He completed the education for him, He said: 'And indeed you are upon a magnificent character' [68:4]. Then He delegated to him the matter of the religion and the community so that he might govern His servants. So He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it' [59:7]. And indeed the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was guided aright, made successful, and supported by the Holy Spirit. He neither slipped nor erred in anything of what he managed in governing the creation. Thus he conducted himself according to the manners of God.

Then indeed God the Mighty and Majestic made obligatory the salat as two rak'ahs, two rak'ahs, being ten rak'ahs (per day). So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) added two rak'ahs to each two, and one rak'ah to al-Maghrib. So these became equal to the obligatory, and it is not permissible to omit them except during a journey; and he left the single rak'ah of al-Maghrib standing (unchanged) in both journey and residency. So God the Mighty and Majestic authorized all of that for him, and the obligatory prayers became seventeen rak'ahs. Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) instituted the supererogatory prayers as thirty-four rak'ahs, double the obligatory. So God the Mighty and Majestic authorized that for him. And the obligatory and the supererogatory are fifty-one rak'ahs, among them two rak'ahs after the falling of darkness performed seated, counted as one rak'ah in the place of al-Witr.

And God made obligatory in the year the fast of the month of Ramadan; and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) instituted fasting in Sha'ban and three days every month — equal to twice the obligatory. So God the Mighty and Majestic authorized that for him. And God the Mighty and Majestic prohibited wine specifically; and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited every intoxicant from all drinks. So God authorized all of that for him.

And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) found certain things repugnant and disliked them, but did not forbid them with the forbiddance of the prohibited (haram). Rather, he forbade them with the forbiddance of repugnance and dislike, then permitted them. So acting upon his permissions became obligatory upon the servants just as obligatory as acting upon his prohibitions and firm resolutions. And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did not grant permission in what he had forbidden as prohibited, nor in what he had commanded as an obligatory necessity. Thus, large quantities of intoxicants from drinks — he forbade them with the forbiddance of the prohibited; he did not permit it for anyone. And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did not permit anyone to shorten the two rak'ahs which he had joined to what God the Mighty and Majestic had made obligatory; rather he made that binding upon them as a binding obligation. He did not permit anyone regarding anything of that, except for the traveler. And it is not for anyone to permit something that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did not permit.

Thus, the commands of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) were in accord with the commands of God the Mighty and Majestic, and his prohibitions with the prohibitions of God the Mighty and Majestic. And it became obligatory upon the servants to submit to him as the submission to God, the Blessed and Exalted.

key_terms.تَفْوِيض: Delegation/authorization — the doctrine that God delegated legislative authority to the Prophet
key_terms.خُلُق عَظِيم: Magnificent character — Quranic praise of the Prophet (68:4)
key_terms.عَزَائِم: Firm resolutions/determinations — binding obligations as opposed to permissions
key_terms.مُسَدَّد: One guided/directed aright — describing the Prophet's infallibility in governance
key_terms.نَافِلَة: Supererogatory prayer — voluntary beyond the obligatory

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic doctrine of tafwid (delegation of authority to the Prophet) according to Imam Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Sadiq (AS) explains the theological basis of the Prophet's legislative authority (tafwid) to Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who was addressing a companion of the rationalist scholar Qays al-Masir. The Imam demonstrates that God educated and perfected the Prophet's character (citing Quran 68:4), then delegated to him authority over religious governance (citing 59:7). The Prophet's additions to worship — extending prayers from 10 to 17 obligatory rak'ahs, instituting supererogatory prayers to reach 51 total, adding fasts in Sha'ban and three days monthly, and extending the prohibition of intoxicants — were all divinely ratified and carry the same binding authority as divine commands. Obedience to the Prophet is thus equivalent to obedience to God.
